title: mLR: Scalable Laminography Reconstruction based on Memoization
problem: ADMM-FFT iterative reconstruction method for laminography has high accuracy but suffers from excessive computation time and large memory consumption due to repeated FFT operations.
motivation: Reduce computation time and memory consumption by exploiting redundancy in FFT operations, enabling larger problem sizes previously infeasible.
method: The algorithm reconstructs 3D laminography images using an iterative method called ADMM-FFT, which repeatedly performs expensive mathematical transformations (FFTs, which convert data between different frequency representations). The key insight is that many of these FFT operations are similar, so instead of recalculating them each time, the system saves the results in memory and reuses them—a technique called memoization. To avoid overflowing CPU memory, intermediate data is moved to graphics processors (GPUs), a technique called variable offloading. The computation is then distributed across multiple GPUs on the same machine and across different machines in a cluster.
key_novelty: Memoization of repeated FFT operations in the ADMM-FFT iterative algorithm, combined with variable offloading to GPUs to reduce CPU memory usage and enable multi-GPU scaling.
contributions: Memoization technique for eliminating redundant FFT computations
Variable offloading strategy for CPU memory reduction
Enables reconstruction on 2K×2K×2K problems (largest ever with ADMM-FFT)
limitations: No comparison with alternative reconstruction methods. Specific GPU platforms not mentioned.
primary_theme: GPU-Accelerated Laminography via Memoization and Offloading
